tail_analysis.reading: THE TYPICAL EVENT LOSES MONEY. Median -4.49% vs SPY over a quarter; 40% positive. The +1.19% mean is entirely a 10% right tail -- 40 events summing to +3,427%, seven times the total positive mass. Remove them and the other 366 average -8.05%. This is a losing strategy with a lottery-ticket tail, not a signal with noise around it. It worsened with more data exactly as a null does: spec #1 median -0.17% -> spec #2 -4.49%, hit rate 49% -> 40%. Not tradeable in reverse either: the +269% events are what a short book cannot survive. No instrument improvement fixes this -- matched controls, winsorizing, fixing survivorship, a longer horizon, a larger sample all push the median DOWN. The problem is the shape of the outcome distribution, not the measurement of it. And the universe is survivor-biased upward, so the true median is worse than -4.49%.
tail_analysis.implication_for_spec_3: Any hypothesis that is a bet on WHICH small company recovers will have this shape. A third specification must have a mechanism where the MEDIAN outcome is positive -- slow information diffusion (post-earnings drift) or a mechanical flow (index-deletion rebound), not a fundamental bet on survival. Filters on insider buying -- officers only, larger threshold, first buy in N years -- are variations on a distribution that has now failed at two horizons and two sample sizes, not new hypotheses.

deviations.cause: The e1 job resolved QT_EVENTS_CSV as `inputs.events_csv || 'data/events/events_form4_1095d.csv'`. But `events_csv` is a dispatch input shared with the count job, whose DECLARED DEFAULT is the v1 file -- so on every dispatch it is non-empty and the fallback never fires. Same failure class as `if typ and typ not in ...`: a fallback that cannot trigger. Caught because 'dropped 51 / wrote 127 / 27 unmatured' matched check 2 on the v1 set to the digit.
